title: The Slave and the Lion
author: Aesop (trans. V. S. Vernon Jones)
summary: 奴隶为狮子拔刺，后来在竞技场上被这头狮子认了出来。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this translation by V. S. Vernon Jones was published in 1912. Public domain in the United States and in China.

paragraphs.en: A Slave ran away from his master, by whom he had been most cruelly treated, and, in order to avoid capture, betook himself into the desert. As he wandered about in search of food and shelter, he came to a cave, which he entered and found to be unoccupied. Really, however, it was a Lion's den, and almost immediately, to the horror of the wretched fugitive, the Lion himself appeared.
paragraphs.zh: 一个奴隶不堪主人残酷的虐待，逃了出来，为了不被抓住，躲进了沙漠。他四处流浪，寻找食物和栖身之处，来到一个山洞，走进去发现里面空无一人。可实际上那是狮子的巢穴，几乎就在同时，那头狮子出现了，把这可怜的逃亡者吓得魂飞魄散。

paragraphs.en: The man gave himself up for lost: but, to his utter astonishment, the Lion, instead of springing upon him and devouring him, came and fawned upon him, at the same time whining and lifting up his paw. Observing it to be much swollen and inflamed, he examined it and found a large thorn embedded in the ball of the foot. He accordingly removed it and dressed the wound as well as he could: and in course of time it healed up completely. The Lion's gratitude was unbounded; he looked upon the man as his friend, and they shared the cave for some time together.
paragraphs.zh: 那人以为自己必死无疑；可令他万分惊讶的是，狮子并没有扑上来吃他，而是走过来蹭他，一边呜咽，一边抬起爪子。他见爪子肿得厉害、发炎了，便仔细查看，发现脚掌里扎着一根大刺。他把刺拔出来，尽力包扎伤口；过了一段时间，伤完全好了。狮子对他感激不尽，把他当作朋友，他们一起在山洞里住了一段时间。

paragraphs.en: A day came, however, when the Slave began to long for the society of his fellow-men, and he bade farewell to the Lion and returned to the town. Here he was presently recognised and carried off in chains to his former master, who resolved to make an example of him, and ordered that he should be thrown to the beasts at the next public spectacle in the theatre.
paragraphs.zh: 然而有一天，奴隶开始思念同类，便告别狮子，回到城里。他很快被人认出，戴上镣铐押回原主人那里。主人决定杀一儆百，下令在下一场公开的剧场表演中把他扔给野兽。

paragraphs.en: On the fatal day the beasts were loosed into the arena, and among the rest a Lion of huge bulk and ferocious aspect; and then the wretched Slave was cast in among them. What was the amazement of the spectators, when the Lion after one glance bounded up to him and lay down at his feet with every expression of affection and delight! It was his old friend of the cave! The audience clamoured that the Slave's life should be spared: and the governor of the town, marvelling at such gratitude and fidelity in a beast, decreed that both should receive their liberty.
paragraphs.zh: 行刑那天，野兽被放进竞技场，其中有一头体型巨大、面目凶猛的狮子；随后，可怜的奴隶被扔到它们中间。令观众惊叹的是，那头狮子只看了他一眼，就纵身跳到他面前，满怀亲昵和喜悦地趴在他脚边！正是他在山洞里的老朋友！观众大声要求饶奴隶一命；城里的总督惊叹于野兽竟如此感恩忠诚，便下令释放他们两人。
